synopsis: The credibility package is broader than simulation results: it must establish context of use, requirements traceability, criteria declared in advance, independent physical evidence, a validity envelope, failed-test disposition and residual risk; internal engineering confidence alone does not guarantee an acceptable dossier [f12291, f1988]. Decision makers expect best estimates, uncertainty statements, factor-by-factor credibility assessments and explicit limitations, with calibration, validation and withheld confirmation data separated and failed validation cases retained [f193, f7587, f7590]. For heavy off-road work, the recommended file records sensor and machine configurations, reference-instrument uncertainty, environmental conditions, acceptance thresholds, invalid regions and validation-data tuning, while the validity record distinguishes physically validated, interpolated and extrapolated regions [f4840, f8012, f8019]. Acceptance precedents requiring dossiers, physical-to-virtual correlation and verification are on-road evidence, and sensor-realism publications lack a common reporting format, leaving a need to identify the accepting authority and agree the evidence approach early [f1564, f6928, f4836, f1987, f7592]. A program starting in October 2026 can realistically have an assessor-seen dossier by mid-2027; the proposed August–September 2027 release gate requires an envelope, limitations and residual uncertainty, and permits release, restricted release or withholding [f69, f10201]. All seven reviewers should receive a one-page credibility map linking claims, evidence types, validating real-world data and responsibility for remaining uncertainty; late exposure of the credibility argument risks rejection, and reproducibility and traceable evidence retention are expected [f10907, f11038, f9997, f10706].
